Keep every row in order. Preserve all [[I]], [[B]], [[SC]] emphasis markers, [[Nnumber]] note markers and explicit source line counts. Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "David Copperfield", "unit": 25, "heading": "CHAPTER 23. I CORROBORATE Mr. DICK, AND CHOOSE A PROFESSION", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "en85-u025-b0030", "target": "Если бы я успел с тех пор, как мы расстались, объехать вокруг света, мы вряд ли могли бы больше обрадоваться новой встрече. Тётка расплакалась в голос, обнимая меня, и сказала, делая вид, будто смеётся, что если бы моя бедная мать была жива, эта глупенькая малютка, без сомнения, тоже пролила бы слёзы.", "source_sha256": "bae9e658c3197d74b04a9af3f7e30c4c1a4c100a7200df9c325f316318740668", "target_id": "ru-en85-u025-b0030", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "3a20c571047fa26458b236c7899a36e0679fc34f926a48604de6ffbcca28ec46"}, {"source_id": "en85-u025-b0031", "target": "— Так вы оставили мистера Дика дома, тётя? — сказал я. — Жаль. А, Джанет, как поживаете?", "source_sha256": "01e4b51b511811d25b095630d03a6727dbe14ae17f6c70bb3915febcd00eb4ec", "target_id": "ru-en85-u025-b0031", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "06539fc85b9f25d418514c4b5b27d1287cd83a3c8402fdddc3ec05330c827526"}], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 23, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u025-b0032", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "As Janet curtsied, hoping I was well, I observed my aunt’s visage lengthen very much.", "sha256": "985eb8628e1664d4306eb4f1d7b37aec389793603d51159ef4ccb4c825d11e96", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[32]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0033", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I am sorry for it, too,’ said my aunt, rubbing her nose. ‘I have had no peace of mind, Trot, since I have been here.’ Before I could ask why, she told me.", "sha256": "fee4dfcb630581c6371dc0ff1e1e6c1969aede2cdfc6e2c467d1ed137ea49a5d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[33]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0034", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I am convinced,’ said my aunt, laying her hand with melancholy firmness on the table, ‘that Dick’s character is not a character to keep the donkeys off. I am confident he wants strength of purpose. I ought to have left Janet at home, instead, and then my mind might perhaps have been at ease. If ever there was a donkey trespassing on my green,’ said my aunt, with emphasis, ‘there was one this afternoon at four o’clock. A cold feeling came over me from head to foot, and I know it was a donkey!’", "sha256": "ab03546571a44de6561f67b6bcf80eef273bbebff82917742399ed62cca3af1d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[34]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0035", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I tried to comfort her on this point, but she rejected consolation.", "sha256": "1957485170ba8e5a5530f6b9838981303c800f8c2a75d3432ca1b35f9b4d16e3", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[35]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0036", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘It was a donkey,’ said my aunt; ‘and it was the one with the stumpy tail which that Murdering sister of a woman rode, when she came to my house.’ This had been, ever since, the only name my aunt knew for Miss Murdstone. ‘If there is any Donkey in Dover, whose audacity it is harder to me to bear than another’s, that,’ said my aunt, striking the table, ‘is the animal!’", "sha256": "acc091c353182f6f155208b3f64e800d9e5d890dfdb3e61b913cf1cbbbee5dd5", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[36]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0037", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Janet ventured to suggest that my aunt might be disturbing herself unnecessarily, and that she believed the donkey in question was then engaged in the sand-and-gravel line of business, and was not available for purposes of trespass. But my aunt wouldn’t hear of it.", "sha256": "ed6ef17a7862008ed978abab0fcc006f9b171296bc1933ad82732b7e66e5570b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[37]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0038", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Supper was comfortably served and hot, though my aunt’s rooms were very high up—whether that she might have more stone stairs for her money, or might be nearer to the door in the roof, I don’t know—and consisted of a roast fowl, a steak, and some vegetables, to all of which I did ample justice, and which were all excellent. But my aunt had her own ideas concerning London provision, and ate but little.", "sha256": "b517110c65e734c94a3492aae5468d8d2ed9f3160bfe8883ac5144c4fe18073a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[38]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0039", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I suppose this unfortunate fowl was born and brought up in a cellar,’ said my aunt, ‘and never took the air except on a hackney coach-stand. I hope the steak may be beef, but I don’t believe it. Nothing’s genuine in the place, in my opinion, but the dirt.’", "sha256": "5a89d8e350c9d68dab67077b3859a6969d61806d1d7f224424c949bd21fb8b65", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[39]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0040", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Don’t you think the fowl may have come out of the country, aunt?’ I hinted.", "sha256": "4f7dc5a9fe42f91e01123c06a499ae643ed7e6475a4dbf0c576cc243090ba6c5", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[40]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0041", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Certainly not,’ returned my aunt. ‘It would be no pleasure to a London tradesman to sell anything which was what he pretended it was.’", "sha256": "4a13d65708a1976285d4240bae68eb98b827890b8f1b3589600edb961200e337", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[41]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0042", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I did not venture to controvert this opinion, but I made a good supper, which it greatly satisfied her to see me do. When the table was cleared, Janet assisted her to arrange her hair, to put on her nightcap, which was of a smarter construction than usual (‘in case of fire’, my aunt said), and to fold her gown back over her knees, these being her usual preparations for warming herself before going to bed. I then made her, according to certain established regulations from which no deviation, however slight, could ever be permitted, a glass of hot wine and water, and a slice of toast cut into long thin strips. With these accompaniments we were left alone to finish the evening, my aunt sitting opposite to me drinking her wine and water; soaking her strips of toast in it, one by one, before eating them; and looking benignantly on me, from among the borders of her nightcap.", "sha256": "56e80daa19252e7bcf77e08fabbf9f006a0a85cf5100d6fb6c6103099d06c36f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[42]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0043", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Well, Trot,’ she began, ‘what do you think of the proctor plan? Or have you not begun to think about it yet?’", "sha256": "c94dc3aacaf2fd3927ab40354e770df23e785a6e4848b1cca15b437fea78804c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[43]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0044", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I have thought a good deal about it, my dear aunt, and I have talked a good deal about it with Steerforth. I like it very much indeed. I like it exceedingly.’", "sha256": "8e3d0a3db2c6e3fac497709829da9fb1601c25e68941e379f145d0b26f4a0d5e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[44]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0045", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Come!’ said my aunt. ‘That’s cheering!’", "sha256": "03119f855754999139ebc6d5a0527e8b5e56cf5f1065b41dcbeec4ce5e6c8428", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[45]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0046", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I have only one difficulty, aunt.’", "sha256": "6f485baa8cc199c2506c8e063833918bbc2771e4088e1acf746d0b476e360f87", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[46]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0047", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Say what it is, Trot,’ she returned.", "sha256": "9f7380dcdd46c4d09f0ed49de37ad9e0cbd1659fb83d5250c3028e2fc4048197", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[47]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0048", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Why, I want to ask, aunt, as this seems, from what I understand, to be a limited profession, whether my entrance into it would not be very expensive?’", "sha256": "005ca1d3c4180ce95194ee579fd6fe181a705dd2a981bcba0bc8c00d37b539bf", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[48]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0049", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘It will cost,’ returned my aunt, ‘to article you, just a thousand pounds.’", "sha256": "df1850cf88dbe88b263eb7d48d98c04256bd61f99d87ffac73a901e91b23df0c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[49]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0050", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Now, my dear aunt,’ said I, drawing my chair nearer, ‘I am uneasy in my mind about that. It’s a large sum of money. You have expended a great deal on my education, and have always been as liberal to me in all things as it was possible to be. You have been the soul of generosity. Surely there are some ways in which I might begin life with hardly any outlay, and yet begin with a good hope of getting on by resolution and exertion. Are you sure that it would not be better to try that course? Are you certain that you can afford to part with so much money, and that it is right that it should be so expended? I only ask you, my second mother, to consider. Are you certain?’", "sha256": "1dccfc9210f519b53206750ba7171aafb99ccdfb0695fa31396b6606185e70e1", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[50]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0051", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "My aunt finished eating the piece of toast on which she was then engaged, looking me full in the face all the while; and then setting her glass on the chimney-piece, and folding her hands upon her folded skirts, replied as follows:", "sha256": "beb82cd6c8cd114353402b880d9de0ab812421c6af42d57b5d75daa3a4787e3e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[51]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0052", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Trot, my child, if I have any object in life, it is to provide for your being a good, a sensible, and a happy man. I am bent upon it—so is Dick. I should like some people that I know to hear Dick’s conversation on the subject. Its sagacity is wonderful. But no one knows the resources of that man’s intellect, except myself!’", "sha256": "c58c82b0b1b60e267c6a208a16f4429e9134f1ed5a4ca7eb3ce3d58f663cec19", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[52]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0053", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "She stopped for a moment to take my hand between hers, and went on:", "sha256": "da8747729aaa4cc209602fd98bcc09e0b3e1371e437d23e64d9f82dc0b59583b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[53]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0054", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘It’s in vain, Trot, to recall the past, unless it works some influence upon the present. Perhaps I might have been better friends with your poor father. Perhaps I might have been better friends with that poor child your mother, even after your sister Betsey Trotwood disappointed me. When you came to me, a little runaway boy, all dusty and way-worn, perhaps I thought so. From that time until now, Trot, you have ever been a credit to me and a pride and a pleasure. I have no other claim upon my means; at least’—here to my surprise she hesitated, and was confused—‘no, I have no other claim upon my means—and you are my adopted child. Only be a loving child to me in my age, and bear with my whims and fancies; and you will do more for an old woman whose prime of life was not so happy or conciliating as it might have been, than ever that old woman did for you.’", "sha256": "4bf3707cc258be143d0231413e99557b7b9d3b3ec04a98c774c1ed33bb348ec3", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[54]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0055", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "It was the first time I had heard my aunt refer to her past history. There was a magnanimity in her quiet way of doing so, and of dismissing it, which would have exalted her in my respect and affection, if anything could.", "sha256": "b4be12541618b638b0c7ab6c2af34b734922ff5be3aaa0b69fe068495a2d1ed6", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[55]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0056", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘All is agreed and understood between us, now, Trot,’ said my aunt, ‘and we need talk of this no more. Give me a kiss, and we’ll go to the Commons after breakfast tomorrow.’", "sha256": "dbb9a493680661221c6cf0a27b053ccfe482f9b3793868289ac6cab043650e4e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[56]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0057", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "We had a long chat by the fire before we went to bed. I slept in a room on the same floor with my aunt’s, and was a little disturbed in the course of the night by her knocking at my door as often as she was agitated by a distant sound of hackney-coaches or market-carts, and inquiring, ‘if I heard the engines?’ But towards morning she slept better, and suffered me to do so too.", "sha256": "d1d0dfd67d5c11873a485f93b42db43c8a8b6fd9d64d36ee07768a4c90357f1e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[57]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0058", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "At about mid-day, we set out for the office of Messrs Spenlow and Jorkins, in Doctors’ Commons. My aunt, who had this other general opinion in reference to London, that every man she saw was a pickpocket, gave me her purse to carry for her, which had ten guineas in it and some silver.", "sha256": "115ec1c278b69a0d85c4699bbd570cdc185a26dc38c1cdb8d02b5730232b6f73", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[58]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0059", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "We made a pause at the toy shop in Fleet Street, to see the giants of Saint Dunstan’s strike upon the bells—we had timed our going, so as to catch them at it, at twelve o’clock—and then went on towards Ludgate Hill, and St. Paul’s Churchyard. We were crossing to the former place, when I found that my aunt greatly accelerated her speed, and looked frightened. I observed, at the same time, that a lowering ill-dressed man who had stopped and stared at us in passing, a little before, was coming so close after us as to brush against her.", "sha256": "84b1ffc1e1dfd8ee99d4ba1a8e1ec5d9d30984b1318ce06e25a0782dac527c84", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[59]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0060", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Trot! My dear Trot!’ cried my aunt, in a terrified whisper, and pressing my arm. ‘I don’t know what I am to do.’", "sha256": "28830d747482ccebab01ba19ec64c5d36cc698d806f7024b89a3264bf253a7d7", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[60]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0061", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Don’t be alarmed,’ said I. ‘There’s nothing to be afraid of. Step into a shop, and I’ll soon get rid of this fellow.’", "sha256": "07bd85f1467ed260bf49b8e59c499d4d9c7d25e90e228fa54e96c6bcc4acd106", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[61]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0062", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘No, no, child!’ she returned. ‘Don’t speak to him for the world. I entreat, I order you!’", "sha256": "8aac5b33c86782b166fd63c938dc6557e46fc557e48f434435a5d7b20967f9eb", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[62]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u025-b0063", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Good Heaven, aunt!’ said I. ‘He is nothing but a sturdy beggar.’", "sha256": "194c99c180d67d177e00f6e497d349bbebd890a812b44c6c6aac7cffac8e627c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[30]/p[63]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}]}
